title_as_printed: Table I (equilibrium gas pressures of dissolved gases at hydrostatic pressures P = 102, 68, 34 and 0 atm.)

footnotes_as_printed.a: P = Hydrostatic pressure; p = gas equilibrium pressure.

pressure_note: p = gas equilibrium pressure (mm Hg, read on a mercury manometer) measured by a null-point method in a Teflon tube immersed in the pressure chamber; 'the vapor pressure corresponding to the water temperatures was subtracted from all gas pressure values', i.e. gas partial pressure. P (capital) is the hydrostatic pressure on the water (1500 p.s.i.g. = 102 atm.), a separate variable. The P column mapped below is the equilibrium gas pressure at zero gauge hydrostatic pressure. The printed partial molal volume is an average over hydrostatic pressures 0-102 atm (straight lines of ln p vs P) and is not a value at the mapped gas pressure.

P.col: p in mm. at P = 0 atm.

value.what: average partial molal volume of the dissolved gas calculated by the authors from the slope of ln p against hydrostatic pressure (their eq. 3)

value2.what: natural log of ratio of equilibrium pressures at hydrostatic 102 atm and 0 atm, read from fitted straight lines in each run

composition.other_species: distilled water (gas-extracted) except rows set by group_rows: 'O2 in sea water' (sea water, composition not given) and 'N2 in detergent' (detergent solution, surface tension 30% of water's)

sets.value: detergent solution, surface tension 30% of water

extra_unmapped: p in mm. at P = 102 atm.
p in mm. at P = 68 atm.
p in mm. at P = 34 atm. (raw equilibrium pressures at elevated hydrostatic pressure P; the measured raw data, not representable as value/P)
conversion_needs: temperature 25 C stated in text ('In all experiments except one, the water temperature was 25 C'); the 0.5 C row is printed as 'O2 at 0.5 degrees'
notes: Rows are 0-based over all CSV rows after the header, label rows included: 0 label O2, 1-4 O2 data, 5 label O2 at 0.5 C, 6 data, 7 label O2 in sea water, 8 data, 9 label N2, 10-12 data, 13 label N2 in detergent, 14 data, 15 label Ar, 16-17 data, 18 label He, 19-20 data, 21 label CO2, 22-23 data. Gas labels are printed beside the first data row; written as separate label rows. The gas pressure at P = 0 is the equilibrium pressure of a solution made at nominally atmospheric gas pressure; dissolved concentrations are not given in the paper. Paper does not define standard conditions (no gas volumes reported).

row_held.reason: O2 in sea water: composition not stated
N2 in detergent solution (surface tension 30% of water): not a pure-water or six-ion brine

quality_remarks: The partial molal volume is an average over hydrostatic pressure 0-102 atm ('average values based on straight lines'), derived by the authors from their equilibrium pressures; all gases except helium give slightly curved plots. Rows 8 (sea water, composition not stated) and 14 (detergent solution) are held.
